results.name: ZMod.val_natCast
results.source_text:
@[simp]
theorem val_natCast (n a : ℕ) : (a : ZMod n).val = a % n := by
  cases n
  · rw [Nat.mod_zero]
    exact Int.natAbs_natCast a
  · apply Fin.val_natCast

results.name: ZMod.val
results.source_text:
/-- `val a` is a natural number defined as:
  - for `a : ZMod 0` it is the absolute value of `a`
  - for `a : ZMod n` with `0 < n` it is the least natural number in the equivalence class

See `ZMod.valMinAbs` for a variant that takes values in the integers.
-/
def val : ∀ {n : ℕ}, ZMod n → ℕ
  | 0 => Int.natAbs
  | n + 1 => ((↑) : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ)
results.docstring:
`val a` is a natural number defined as:
- for `a : ZMod 0` it is the absolute value of `a`
- for `a : ZMod n` with `0 < n` it is the least natural number in the equivalence class

See `ZMod.valMinAbs` for a variant that takes values in the integers.

results.name: ZMod.natCast_zmod_val
results.source_text:
/-- So-named because the coercion is `Nat.cast` into `ZMod`. For `Nat.cast` into an arbitrary ring,
see `ZMod.natCast_val`. -/
theorem natCast_zmod_val {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (a : ZMod n) : (a.val : ZMod n) = a := by
  cases n
  · cases NeZero.ne 0 rfl
  · apply Fin.cast_val_eq_self
results.docstring:
So-named because the coercion is `Nat.cast` into `ZMod`. For `Nat.cast` into an arbitrary ring,
see `ZMod.natCast_val`.

results.name: Mathlib.Meta.NormNum.evalNatCast
results.source_text:
/-- The `norm_num` extension which identifies an expression `Nat.cast n`, returning `n`. -/
@[norm_num Nat.cast _, NatCast.natCast _] def evalNatCast : NormNumExt where eval {u α} e := do
  let sα ← inferAddMonoidWithOne α
  let .app n (a : Q(ℕ)) ← whnfR e | failure
  guard <|← withNewMCtxDepth <| isDefEq n q(Nat.cast (R := $α))
  let ⟨na, pa⟩ ← deriveNat a q(Nat.instAddMonoidWithOne)
  haveI' : $e =Q $a := ⟨⟩
  return .isNat sα na q(isNat_natCast $a $na $pa)
results.docstring: The `norm_num` extension which identifies an expression `Nat.cast n`, returning `n`.

results.name: PMF.toOuterMeasure
results.source_text:
/-- Construct an `OuterMeasure` from a `PMF`, by assigning measure to each set `s : Set α` equal
  to the sum of `p x` for each `x ∈ α`. -/
def toOuterMeasure (p : PMF α) : OuterMeasure α :=
  OuterMeasure.sum fun x : α => p x • dirac x
results.docstring:
Construct an `OuterMeasure` from a `PMF`, by assigning measure to each set `s : Set α` equal
to the sum of `p x` for each `x ∈ α`.

results.name: Module.FinitePresentation
results.source_text:
/--
A module is finitely presented if it is finitely generated by some set `s`
and the kernel of the presentation `Rˢ → M` is also finitely generated.
-/
class Module.FinitePresentation : Prop where
  out : ∃ (s : Finset M), Submodule.span R (s : Set M) = ⊤ ∧
    (LinearMap.ker (Finsupp.linearCombination R ((↑) : s → M))).FG
results.docstring:
A module is finitely presented if it is finitely generated by some set `s`
and the kernel of the presentation `Rˢ → M` is also finitely generated.

results.name: Algebra.FinitePresentation
results.source_text:
/-- An algebra over a commutative semiring is `Algebra.FinitePresentation` if it is the quotient of
a polynomial ring in `n` variables by a finitely generated ideal. -/
class Algebra.FinitePresentation [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] : Prop where
  out : ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R →ₐ[R] A), Surjective f ∧ (RingHom.ker f.toRingHom).FG
results.docstring:
An algebra over a commutative semiring is `Algebra.FinitePresentation` if it is the quotient of
a polynomial ring in `n` variables by a finitely generated ideal.

results.name: UnitDependent
results.source_text:
/-- A type carries the instance `UnitDependent M` if it depends on a choice of units.
  This dependence is manifested in `scaleUnit u1 u2` which describes how elements of `M` change
  under a scaling of units which would take `u1` to `u2`.

  This type is used for functions, and propositions etc.
-/
class UnitDependent (M : Type) where
  /-- `scaleUnit u1 u2` is the map transforming elements of `M` under a
    scaling of units which would take the unit `u1` to the unit `u2`. This is not
    to say that in `scaleUnit u1 u2 m` that `m` should be interpreted as being in the units `u1`,
    although this is often the case.
  -/
  scaleUnit : UnitChoices → UnitChoices → M → M
  scaleUnit_trans : ∀ u1 u2 u3 m, scaleUnit u2 u3 (scaleUnit u1 u2 m) = scaleUnit u1 u3 m
  scaleUnit_trans' : ∀ u1 u2 u3 m, scaleUnit u1 u2 (scaleUnit u2 u3 m) = scaleUnit u1 u3 m
  scaleUnit_id : ∀ u m, scaleUnit u u m = m
results.docstring:
A type carries the instance `UnitDependent M` if it depends on a choice of units.
This dependence is manifested in `scaleUnit u1 u2` which describes how elements of `M` change
under a scaling of units which would take `u1` to `u2`.

This type is used for functions, and propositions etc.

results.name: LinearUnitDependent
results.source_text:
/--
  A type `M` with an instance of `UnitDependent M` such that `scaleUnit u1 u2` is compatible
  with the `Module ℝ M` instance on `M`.
-/
class LinearUnitDependent (M : Type) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℝ M] extends UnitDependent M where
  scaleUnit_add : ∀ u1 u2 m1 m2,
    scaleUnit u1 u2 (m1 + m2) = scaleUnit u1 u2 m1 + scaleUnit u1 u2 m2
  scaleUnit_smul : ∀ u1 u2 (r : ℝ) m,
    scaleUnit u1 u2 (r • m) = r • scaleUnit u1 u2 m
results.docstring:
A type `M` with an instance of `UnitDependent M` such that `scaleUnit u1 u2` is compatible
with the `Module ℝ M` instance on `M`.

results.name: LinearUnitDependent.scaleUnitLinearEquiv
results.source_text:
/-- For an `M` with an instance of `LinearUnitDependent M`, `scaleUnit u1 u2` as a
  linear equivalence. -/
def LinearUnitDependent.scaleUnitLinearEquiv {M : Type} [AddCommMonoid M]
    [Module ℝ M] [LinearUnitDependent M] (u1 u2 : UnitChoices) :
    M ≃ₗ[ℝ] M :=
    LinearEquiv.ofLinear (scaleUnitLinear u1 u2) (scaleUnitLinear u2 u1)
    (by ext u; simp [scaleUnitLinear])
    (by ext u; simp [scaleUnitLinear])
results.docstring:
For an `M` with an instance of `LinearUnitDependent M`, `scaleUnit u1 u2` as a
linear equivalence.

results.name: isDimensionallyCorrect_iff
results.source_text:
lemma isDimensionallyCorrect_iff {M : Type} [UnitDependent M] (m : M) :
    IsDimensionallyCorrect m ↔ ∀ u1 u2 : UnitChoices,
      scaleUnit u1 u2 m = m := by rfl
